preferred_denominator: Author-calculated sum of FEMA NRI v1.20 wildfire building-value Expected Annual Loss (WFIR_EALB)
unit: US dollars per year, December 2024 price basis

source_fields.WFIR_EALB: Wildfire - Expected Annual Loss - Building Value
source_fields.WFIR_EALT: Wildfire - Expected Annual Loss - Total; includes population-equivalence and agriculture, do not substitute for WFIR_EALB

methodology.frequency_model: FEMA hazard-info table directly reports Wildfire PeriodOfRecord = 2024 dataset, FrequencyModel = Probability; do not describe as a single observed year.
methodology.hazard_simulation: Technical chapter22 describes FSim simulation of many hypothetical contemporary seasons under 2024 landscape conditions and management practices, generating probability of large fires that escape initial suppression on a 270m grid.
methodology.loss_calibration: Technical p22-9, Table85: SHELDUS wildfire losses from1996–2023,150Fire-Forest records and3708Wildfire records. Building HLR defaults for counties intersecting flame-intensity-class6 cells are0.3West,0.1Southeast,0.1Northeast; calibrated to regional mean annual SHELDUS building loss.
methodology.exposure_pricebasis: FEMA ArcGIS metadata: building and population exposures from Hazus6.0, inflation adjusted to December2024 dollars. County boundaries Census2021TIGER, exceptConnecticut2024TIGER.
methodology.building_definition_limit: The directly verified field is building-value EAL. I have not established an explicit source statement excluding contents or business interruption from SHELDUS calibration. Therefore call it building-value EAL, not a precisely isolated structural-replacement or insured-property-loss account. It is clearly separate from population/agriculture consequences in the data.
methodology.aggregation: Fetch all3232 county/equivalent rows in two API pages, filter50states+DC (3144 rows), sum WFIR_EALB. All88 territorial rows have zero wildfire building EAL, so includingthem leaves the same sum. The sum is an author calculation, not a FEMA-published national headline.
methodology.no_double_count: Sum county rows only. Never add overlapping census-tract totals, WFIR_EALT, insured payouts, or separate historical property loss estimates.

reproducibility.hazard_info_source_note: The hazard-info service URL is provided above; its source record is not redistributed as a separate snapshot in this package.

model_recommendation: Use L0 = US$3.6745B/year in December2024 dollars as a screening baseline. Apply separately specified eligible-loss share, successful adoption, and incremental loss-reduction effectiveness relative to current management; model R&D success and delay. Do not claim allL0is addressable by plant research. If the scope is California useUS$1.7064B/year; a national rollout cannot also addCalifornia orLA EAL. All model costs must share this real-price basis or be converted transparently.
limitations: Modelled planning baseline, not observed annual damage or an audited expenditure series.
Not property-level underwriting or local engineering risk; county averages conceal within-county variation.
The2025LAcatastrophe is not in the1996–2023loss-calibration record.
Landscape and future climate changes are not automatically forecast by this baseline.
No source establishes an eligible share or wildfire-loss reduction effect for GMO/low-flammability vegetation; those remain scenarios.
